approach.method_basis: The Parent searches from two scored molecular centers. Each region generates new graph-edit paths, fits a count-fingerprint Gaussian process using its own episode's accepted molecules, and competes for evaluations through posterior samples in objective units. Both models already use one response amplitude estimated from the session's accepted archive. Real regional improvements drive the existing expansion, contraction and restart counters; an unpurchased region receives no update. Restarted regions begin with a singleton fit and an already observed root.
approach.novelty: Add minimal final-slot regional feedback coverage. Keep the first nine auction purchases, then use the last existing posterior sample to buy from a feasible region that has no purchase yet. This gives an otherwise idle local search one real observation with which its unchanged model and controller can adapt. Earlier siblings changed restart predictor context, root separation or the success reference; this intervention changes only continued access to paid feedback. It may also waste the final slot, so useful later refinement and the complete endpoint panel must justify the diversion.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting Parent behavior is continued regional feedback drought after successful initial exposure. The complete n-7d1e6230ecce Search panel contains 435 auctions and 870 regional boundaries, of which 347 buy nothing; the longest observed drought spans all 29 announcements. All 19 natural resets nevertheless receive immediate accepted purchases, so blanket reset starvation is not the bottleneck. Read-only reconstruction of every original auction from its actual raw sample rows reproduces all selections; applying only the frozen final-slot coverage rule keeps the first nine identical in every batch, changes exactly 347 final identities and covers both feasible regions in every reconstructed batch. These are action differences only. hypothesis: On the shared-amplitude episode-owned regional Parent, constrain only the final purchase's eligibility when a feasible region is still absent from the selected prefix. For announced batch size B and candidate ordering O inherited from the Parent, retain the original sample rows and available canonical identities. At positions k < B-1 choose the original global maximum. At k=B-1, form M from regions with zero selected-prefix members and at least one remaining valid novel candidate. If M is nonempty, choose the maximum of that same final sample row among remaining candidates owned by regions in M; otherwise choose the original unrestricted maximum. Preserve first-in-existing-order tie resolution and global identity exclusion. In the frozen two-region batch-ten profile at most one region can be missing after the first nine, and at most the final purchased identity can change. A real accepted final-slot purchase enters the existing episode fit and local-center success/failure law; no missing purchase creates an observation, success or failure. The hypothesized chain is elimination of feasible no-feedback boundaries, more actual local learning/control updates, useful later descendants and improved full/late global conversion. More exposure alone does not establish useful conversion.

finding_summary.headline: Regional feedback drought vanished, but full-run gains fell and the registered utility test failed
finding_summary.insights:
This experiment separates access to observations from productive use of them. The regions can now learn and advance their counters throughout the run, so continued feedback starvation is no longer an explanation for this variant’s weak endpoints. The borrowed forced-access element operated, and the retained separation between selection and paid-data updates operated too. Its finite final-slot adaptation supplies no evidence for the source literature’s age schedule, continuous trust-region geometry or regret guarantees. More paid updates and more restarts did not provide the required finite-budget benefit. Improved late conversion is real, but it did not recover the earlier loss; full increment mass and endpoint score express the same final-minus-initial quantity.

The measured limitation is conversion of the newly purchased regional information into globally useful refinement. Only three of 191 diversions immediately beat the global incumbent, and the union of 478 later accepted descendants contains just four strict global gains totaling 0.008703. Another 129 diversions have no accepted descendant, including five terminal observations for which later use is censored. This does not prove that their labels had no indirect model effect, and the displaced candidates were never evaluated, so the audit cannot assign an actual opportunity cost or identify causal mediation. It narrows the unresolved method question to the quality of regional proposals and their ranking for useful improvement. A proposal operator that can reach distinct complete scaffold/linker arrangements, or a ranking model that estimates their useful improvement, could address that limitation; this node does not establish either remedy.

Molecular evidence explains why broader exploration is insufficient: typed/generic scaffolds increased from 1,880/1,234 to 2,064/1,382, yet one high-score subset of 87 still occupied only 14 typed and eight generic scaffolds and included tied peripheral variants. Both the fragment tail and the oversized tail grew, from 134/245 to 162/262 molecules, while reactive bond environments and unresolved stereochemistry remained. These associations locate proposal-quality limitations, not a proven cause of the score loss or a mandate to remove every unusual group. The finding settles this specific final-slot utility prediction under two feasible regions and batch ten; the wider local-model approach and the isolated contributions of its retained components remain open.
finding_summary.results:
Every region received a real purchase in every batch: paid regional update boundaries rose from 523 of 870 to 870 of 870, and the longest feedback drought fell from 29 batches to zero. All 435 auctions preserved the first nine choices. The final coverage rule applied 197 times, genuinely diverting 191 purchases and leaving six final choices unchanged. All were accepted. The unchanged controller then made 94 contractions and 62 natural restarts, versus 50 and 19 in the Parent. Of the 191 diverted observations, 165 entered a subsequent owned model fit; 21 ended a retired episode and five arrived at the final boundary. They produced 41 local improvements but only three immediate global improvements. Sixty-two had later accepted descendants; those descendants supplied four further chronological global improvements.

Late global gain per evaluation increased from 0.000382624 to 0.000486230, but full-run gain per evaluation decreased from 0.001296971 to 0.001280512. Complete mean endpoint score fell from 0.5846137565 to 0.5798405659, a paired loss of 0.0047731906 instead of the required gain of 0.002. Seven of fifteen task/seed endpoints improved and eight declined; the seed-macro differences were -0.0273125, -0.0018620 and +0.0148549. The Child also remained 0.0271897503 below the formal Anchor. All fifteen sessions completed without evaluator rejection or numerical fallback. Thus execution and real feedback coverage are established, while the registered conjunction of better full and late conversion and endpoint gain is refuted.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich heteroaromatic families retain reactive bonds, unresolved stereochemistry and both fragment and oversized tails.
molecular.overall_character: This assessment covers all five supplied objectives and Search seeds 0, 1 and 2: 4,350 accepted optimizer molecules per node, excluding the fixed initial observations from population counts. The frozen comparison explicitly says child_complete=true and paired_complete=true against code Parent n-7d1e6230ecce; all fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent trajectories were present and read. No comparison path was missing. Child inputs were still staging files under /projects/standard/adeshwal/shared/zhou2577/SPIRAL/.worktrees/slot-2/runs/staging at assessment time, not published node artifacts. The run-relative evidence manifest policy/scratch/r0054-02-improve-L01-molecular/summary.json enumerates every original staging path, its immutable-byte snapshot file, every published Parent trajectory file, SHA-256 hashes, per-cell audits, source identities and descriptor definitions. The request grants the original Child trajectories as SMILES citation authority; the snapshots preserve those same bytes and do not grant additional citation authority. These are evaluated outputs, not a census of unpurchased graph candidates. Rings and aromatic chemistry are abundant: the supplied string-level ring-closure rates range from 0.9506 to 0.9655 and aromatic-presence rates from 0.9172 to 0.9575. These are molecule-level textual presence counters, not aromatic atom fractions. Graph perception gives 4,175 ring-bearing and 4,101 aromatic-bearing Child proposals. Recognizable indole/partially hydrogenated fused-ring carboxamides, fused nitrogen heterocycles, cyclic amines, ethers and carbonyls coexist with N-halogen, O-halogen, peroxide, imine and highly edited ring environments. Median size is 29 heavy atoms, but the range is 1 to 113; 162 proposals have fewer than six heavy atoms and 262 exceed fifty, versus 134 and 245 in the Parent. There is real graph diversity: 2,064 nonempty typed and 1,382 generic Murcko scaffolds versus 1,880 and 1,234 in the Parent. That breadth includes unusual or repeated ring edits and does not establish useful synthetic scaffold diversity. The Child has 972 N-halogen-bearing, 153 O-halogen-bearing and 144 O-O-bearing molecules, compared with 1,017, 104 and 48 in the Parent. Potential tetrahedral centers occur in 2,308 Child molecules, with no assigned centers; the digest independently has zero stereocentre-text rate on every objective. RDKit small all-aromatic ring warnings decrease from 336 to 26; this definition counts perceived rings of at most four atoms whose members are all aromatic, and is not a conformational feasibility test. Thus some structural warning signs decrease while others increase. The plausibility judgment is a chemical reading, not a synthesis-route or activity prediction. High-score associations, Child-Parent differences and graph descriptors do not attribute any chemical change to a controller component.

per_task.generated_character: The dominant recognizable family is a substituted fused aromatic/partially saturated nitrogen ring carrying an aryl carboxamide, methoxy or ethoxy groups, and variable methyl, cyano and halogen substituents. The population median is 25 heavy atoms; the highest-scoring 87 molecules span 23 to 27. The strongest example is a 24-heavy-atom, three-ring methoxy/cyano dihydroquinoline-like carboxanilide. Related indole carboxamides are conventional-looking frameworks, although other seeds supply N-fluoroamides or N-amino amides. There are 316 typed/202 generic nonempty scaffolds versus 298/161 in the published Parent; the two populations retain the same broad aryl-amide ancestry. The Parent has 222 small all-aromatic ring warnings versus nine here, while N-halogen-bearing structures decrease from 414 to 224. These are whole-population differences, not evidence of a specific edit being beneficial.
liabilities: N-halogen bonds remain common even though the cited local N-Cl analogue is weaker; seed-0 and seed-2 leaders include an N-fluoroamide and an N-amino amide respectively.
Very small species and overgrown recombinations coexist with sensible-sized leaders; no synthetic route or 3D feasibility evidence is supplied for the more unusual ring edits.
missing_features: Reliable access to alternative compact fused-ring/carbonyl arrangements that retain the high-scoring cyano/ether/amide architecture without relying on N-halogen or N-amino substitutions is not demonstrated across seeds.

The outputs do not establish a stable, well-defined chemical counterpart for every high-scoring edited scaffold; the trajectories do not identify a unique absent substituent whose addition would improve the objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The cyano/methoxy fused carboxamide at seed 1 evaluation 128 scores 0.5046949386828399; the related indole at evaluation 87 scores 0.4952605565436486. Replacing the fused-ring NH of the former with N-Cl at evaluation 159 gives 0.48660033404583897, so that local comparison does not reward N-chlorination. A 46-heavy-atom recombined structure at seed 1 evaluation 147 scores 4.987806256420767e-22, while FF scores zero. The observed gradient favors a bounded, connected aromatic/carbonyl arrangement over both fragmentation and duplication. Parent-relative endpoints move in mixed directions in the frozen comparison; the largest Child score is below the Parent seed-1 leader, despite fewer small-ring warnings. No missing exact target scaffold can be deduced from these associations.

per_task.generated_character: These are the largest proposals: median 41 heavy atoms, maximum 113, with 209 of 870 above fifty. The seed-1 leader is a 45-heavy-atom, four-ring assembly of a fused nitrogen heteroaromatic/carbocyclic system and a substituted pyridyl group, with multiple alkenes, alkyl/ether groups, F/Br substitution and an N=CH-S-alkyl linkage. Other seed leaders are poly-imine nitrogen heteroaromatics and a five-ring fused carbonyl/thione family. This is rich heterocyclic chemistry, but the crowded, multiply unsaturated and reactive substituent patterns make preparation and isolation questionable. Whole-population scaffold counts are 470 typed/374 generic versus 450/347 in the Parent, whereas the highest-scoring 87 Child proposals occupy only 14 typed/eight generic scaffolds. The corresponding Parent subset has 24/11.
liabilities: Repeated oversized assemblies consume evaluations, and the top family contains multiple unspecified alkene geometries and potential tetrahedral configurations.
The tied O-CH2-Br analogue introduces a reactive bromoalkyl ether without a measured score advantage; N-halogen-bearing molecules number 151 versus 23 in the Parent.
missing_features: The trajectory does not show that elaborate peripheral unsaturation, reactive imine/thioimidate-like groups or bromoalkyl ethers are required for the favorable heterocyclic arrangements; more conventional counterparts remain an untested chemical gap.

Independent, compact heterocyclic architectures with preserved attachment geometry are underrepresented among the leaders relative to the broad full-population graph variation. No exact missing decoration is inferable from the score floor and tied analogues.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fused, extensively decorated seed-1 leader scores 0.644927536231884. A smaller alkene/imine-decorated pyridine at seed 1 evaluation 146 scores 0.5152958657460012; F, CS and other fragments sit at the observed 0.5 floor. The seed-2 fused carbonyl/thione leader scores 0.6134806205800121. Thus several complete heterocyclic architectures outperform fragments, but size alone is insufficient: the 113-heavy-atom repeated structure scores 0.5882571941658272. The best ethoxy structure and its O-CH2-Br analogue tie exactly at 0.644927536231884, showing that a chemically consequential peripheral change can be invisible to the observed score. The Child high-score subset is larger than the Parent subset (median 45 versus 31 heavy atoms), with mixed paired endpoint changes. This is a descriptive shift, not proof that molecular enlargement improves the objective.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest family connects two substituted aromatic groups through a flexible secondary-amine/tertiary-pyrrolidine arrangement. The seed-2 leader has 30 heavy atoms and three rings, with aryl Cl/Br, methylthio and thiophenol groups plus a benzylic carbon bearing both Cl and an amine. Other seeds produce bridged ring aminoalcohol/sulfoxide and larger sulfur-nitrogen-ring analogues. The whole-population median is 33 heavy atoms; the highest-scoring 87 span 27 to 34. Ring and basic-amine chemistry are clearly present, not missing. Relative to the Parent, typed/generic scaffolds increase from 355/234 to 425/285 and the high-score subset median grows from 23 to 31 heavy atoms. These outputs look medicinal-chemistry-like at the scaffold level but frequently retain unusual local functional groups.
liabilities: The best series combines an alpha-amino benzylic chloride with thiol/thioether groups, raising stability and reactivity questions independently of its score.
Sulfur-containing bridged and larger-ring alternatives have no route or conformational validation. The digest reports no charged SMILES here; ionization states and pKa were not measured.
missing_features: Defined stereochemical identities are absent despite potential tetrahedral centers in every molecule in the highest-scoring 87; which configuration would be favored is unmeasured.

The high-scoring diaryl/amine geometry lacks a demonstrated set of equally effective conventional counterparts without benzylic amino-halide, thiol or hemiaminal-like environments. The sample does not support prescribing an absent receptor-specific group.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The diaryl diamine at seed 2 evaluation 254 scores 0.999996008556122; its thiomethyl-substituted analogue at evaluation 261 scores 0.9999923277689723. In contrast, a small aryl sulfur-oxide structure without an amine scores 0.00024675866379847753, and the 25-heavy-atom acidic amide/N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine at seed 2 evaluation 18 scores 0.0005876222816323224. In this observed sample, accessible amine-containing ring/linker architectures with aromatic groups are associated with higher scores than small sulfur fragments or the acidic, amide/sulfonamide-rich early structures. Multiple features change together, so this does not establish an isolated amine effect or receptor binding. The Parent also produces high-scoring amine/ring architectures, with mixed endpoint changes across seeds. The near-unit Child score does not establish chemical stability, affinity or a validated docking pose.

per_task.generated_character: The output combines fused aromatic nitrogen systems, ethers and carbonyl-rich cyclic amines with many enlarged or bridged ring systems. The seed-1 leader has 35 heavy atoms and five rings: a fused aza-aromatic unit linked through an ethoxy chain to a benzene-fused polycyclic amide/urea and methylated amine system. The seed-2 leader instead combines fused dicarbonyl N-O heterocyclic chemistry with an aryl-substituted nitrogen heterocycle and an enlarged diamine ring. The population median is 32 heavy atoms; 489 of 870 have a perceived ring of at least eight atoms. Large rings are not intrinsically impossible, but these edited frameworks need geometric and route assessment. The Child has 591 typed/426 generic nonempty scaffolds versus 607/434 in the Parent. Both explore broad ring topology; lack of rings or nitrogen functionality is not the limitation.
liabilities: O-O bonds occur in 98 proposals and in 22 of the highest-scoring 87; the unusual carbonyl-rich peroxide environments require chemical stability assessment.
Large and bridged heterocycles, repeated scaffold concatenation and unresolved tetrahedral centers complicate synthetic interpretation even where RDKit accepts the connectivity.
missing_features: The sample does not demonstrate broadly accessible, geometrically credible alternative ring/linker arrangements that preserve the higher-scoring aromatic/carbonyl/amine organization; simply increasing ring count is not supported.

Stable counterparts to the O-O and N-O dicarbonyl ring environments and specified configurations of newly stereogenic frameworks are missing from the reported high-score comparison. The score gain from those replacements is unknown.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-1 fused aza-aromatic/amide/amine assembly scores 0.22824773342641633 and the seed-2 N-O heterocyclic analogue scores 0.22639850133566514. A 26-heavy-atom nonaromatic amide/acid/hydroxamate structure scores 0.07630846195841996, while C and SCS score zero. A 78-heavy-atom repeated assembly scores 0.1292851263109029, below the 35-heavy-atom leader: retaining aromatic nitrogen, carbonyl and cyclic-amine arrangements within a bounded architecture is associated with the better values. Nevertheless an O-O-bearing seed-2 final analogue scores 0.21412422900111605, so the observed score tolerates questionable bond environments. Paired endpoints are mixed; small all-aromatic ring warnings fall from 107 to six while O-O-bearing proposals rise from 23 to 98. One liability is exchanged for another rather than a uniformly more credible chemical population.

per_task.generated_character: The recurrent core is a fused nitrogen heteroaromatic dicarbonyl or imino-carbonyl system, elaborated with fluoromethyl groups, fluorinated unsaturated rings and frequent N-F bonds. The strongest seed-1 structure has 28 heavy atoms and three rings, including an aldehyde-substituted cyclopentadiene-like ring attached to the fused heterocycle, an N-F bond and several C-F-bearing side groups. The population median is 26 heavy atoms and the highest-scoring 87 span 23 to 29; 550 of 870 proposals contain N-halogen bonds. The digest also records a cumulated-double-bond text rate of 0.1, consistent with unusual unsaturated alternatives in this population. Scaffold counts rise from the Parent 200 typed/105 generic to 295/153, but both populations continue to favor fluorinated fused nitrogen heterocycles. Broader graph variation does not remove the local chemistry liabilities.
liabilities: N-halogen bonds occur in 72 of the highest-scoring 87 proposals, compared with 60 in the Parent subset; high score clearly does not certify a conventional stable bond environment.
Reactive aldehyde, cumulated unsaturation, repeated polycycles and unspecified stereochemistry accompany otherwise recognizable fused heterocyclic cores.
missing_features: A chemically conventional set of compact fluorinated heterocyclic alternatives preserving the favorable size and heteroatom arrangement without N-F dependence is not established by the leaders.

Specified configurations and less reactive counterparts to the aldehyde/unsaturated-ring environments remain absent from the evaluated comparison; their objective value is unmeasured and cannot be supplied from task identity.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-1 N-F/aldehyde leader scores 0.6314013620592299; replacing that N-F substituent with N-CH2F at evaluation 300 gives 0.6185247699731126. The seed-2 compact phenolic imino-carbonyl analogue scores 0.5789926343641532. A 61-heavy-atom repeated polycycle from seed 1 evaluation 202 scores 2.7559363253766806e-52. The observed gradient therefore rewards particular compact fluorinated heterocyclic arrangements and strongly disfavors some duplicated structures; it does not justify arbitrary fluorination or size growth. The local N-F versus N-CH2F pair actually favors the more questionable N-F environment, so conventional chemistry cannot be assumed to improve this score. The Parent seed-0 leader reaches 0.7327195754462501 with its own unusual N-F-rich ring architecture; the other paired Child endpoints improve. These mixed results do not reveal a unique missing target pharmacophore.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-1cd50f38b9c4, accepted optimizer outputs on frozen Search seeds 0/1/2; paired baseline n-7d1e6230ecce, same panel. The Child has 972 N-halogen-bearing and 153 O-halogen-bearing molecules among 4,350, versus 1,017 and 104 in the Parent; O-O-bearing molecules increase from 48 to 144. Cited high-scoring examples include N-fluoro carbonyl heterocycles, an N-chloro fused-ring amine, an alpha-amino benzylic chloride and peroxide-containing rings. A tied ether/bromoalkyl-ether pair shows score indifference to a chemical liability, while a local N-F/N-CH2F pair favors N-F. Sources and exact structural definitions are retained in policy/scratch/r0054-02-improve-L01-molecular/summary.json.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve conventional local bond chemistry while elaborating otherwise recognizable ring and carbonyl frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic capability would need access to conventional alternative bond environments that preserve a useful scaffold and attachment geometry, with reactivity assessed separately from accepted score. These associations do not establish that blanket removal of every unusual group improves utility, nor that any controller component caused the chemistry change.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-1cd50f38b9c4, frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, evaluated optimizer outputs only: 162 of 4,350 molecules have fewer than six heavy atoms and 262 exceed fifty, against 134 and 245 in code Parent n-7d1e6230ecce. Observed sizes span 1 to 113 heavy atoms. Quoted fragments reach zero or the observed floor, and quoted repeated architectures can be far below their compact relatives. This is not a universal size penalty: the largest population also contains some high-scoring structures above fifty. The complete denominators and input hashes are in policy/scratch/r0054-02-improve-L01-molecular/summary.json.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator cannot consistently vary molecular architecture without collapsing it into fragments or duplicating it into oversized assemblies.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs meaningful scaffold and substituent changes that retain connected functional architecture while allowing size to move in both directions. Use current-session observations to learn where size changes help; these trajectories do not establish a universal hard cutoff or a benefit from rejecting every large or small structure.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-1cd50f38b9c4, accepted outputs from frozen Search seeds 0/1/2: RDKit identifies potential tetrahedral centers in 2,308 of 4,350 molecules but assigned centers in none. Every molecule in one highest-scoring subset of 87 has potential centers, and the supplied digest independently reports zero stereocentre-text rate for all objectives. The paired Parent also has no assigned centers. The exact perception settings and source hashes are recorded in policy/scratch/r0054-02-improve-L01-molecular/summary.json.
transferable_gaps.gap: The emitted structures do not preserve or assign stereochemical identity when graph changes create potential tetrahedral centers.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator supplying concrete chemical candidates would need to represent, preserve and deliberately vary stereochemical identity through edits. Unspecified SMILES do not identify an experimentally resolved stereoisomer. Whether stereochemical search improves the measured objective is untested; no preferred configuration follows from this report.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-1cd50f38b9c4 versus code Parent n-7d1e6230ecce, complete frozen Search panel and evaluated optimizer outputs only: typed/generic nonempty scaffold counts increase from 1,880/1,234 to 2,064/1,382. Yet one highest-scoring subset of 87 has only 14 typed/eight generic scaffolds, and tied leaders differ by peripheral ether/halogen decoration. Unusual ring edits persist: 26 Child molecules contain a perceived all-aromatic ring of at most four atoms, down from 336 in the Parent; other populations shift toward peroxide-containing or enlarged rings. These counts are structural descriptions, not synthetic feasibility or component attribution; sources and definitions are in policy/scratch/r0054-02-improve-L01-molecular/summary.json.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad graph and ring variation is available, but reliable access to distinct, chemically interpretable alternatives around favorable functional arrangements remains limited.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic capability would need to reach alternative complete ring/linker frameworks while retaining functional arrangements supported by current-session observations, and distinguish feasible topology from canonical graph novelty. More Murcko scaffolds, more rings or more peripheral variants alone are not evidence of useful diversity; the utility and chemical credibility of any new access must be checked separately.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
